The use of erythromycin stearate may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when combined with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, such as those causing bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or when co-administered with other QTc-prolonging drugs or in the presence of congenital QT prolongation. Close monitoring is essential. 2. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 3. Erythromycin stearate also increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, dexamethasone decreases erythromycin stearate levels via the same pathway. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. DHEA, a herbal supplement, increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of buccal diazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the elimination rate of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is required. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of intranasal diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 10. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases dihydroergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of intranasal dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Consider an alternative to erythromycin in patients receiving diltiazem. 17. Diltiazem increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Erythromycin stearate and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is contraindicated. Erythromycin stearate also increases disopyramide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin stearate and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Erythromycin stearate and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Erythromycin stearate increases donepezil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 23. Donepezil and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Erythromycin stearate and doxepin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronedarone and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is contraindicated. 28. Erythromycin stearate and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Drospirenone increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 30. Erythromycin stearate increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Duvelisib increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with duvelisib increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing toxicity. Consider reducing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate and monitor for signs of toxicity. 32. Erythromycin stearate increases edoxaban levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 34. Efavirenz decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases elagolix levels through other mechanisms. This interaction is contraindicated. Elagolix increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases eletriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 38. Eliglustat decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Erythromycin stearate increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat poor or intermediate metabolizers; reduce eliglustat dose from 84 mg BID to 84 mg once daily in extensive metabolizers. Eliglustat and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Eluxadoline increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin stearate increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Decrease eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 40. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. 41. Encorafenib increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Encorafenib, an OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of OATP1B3 substrates. Erythromycin stearate increases encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If concomitant use of a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce encorafenib dose to one-half of the dose (e.g., reduce from 450 mg/day to 225 mg/day). Encorafenib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Erythromycin stearate increases enoxaparin effects by inhibiting metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 43. Erythromycin stearate and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate increases entrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the moderate CYP3A inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 44. Enzalutamide decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Epinephrine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Racemic epinephrine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases eplerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erdafitinib increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after administration of P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases ergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Eribulin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases erlotinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Escitalopram increases erythromycin stearate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases estradiol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases estradiol vaginal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 57. Erythromycin stearate increases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It decreases their levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 59. Erythromycin stearate increases esterified estrogens levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It decreases their levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Erythromycin stearate increases esterified estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
